title: October 17, 2003: India launched its heaviest remote-sensing satellite - built to watch its own land from space.

sources.text: Universe Today - India launches remote sensing satellite

caption:
October 17, 2003: India launched its heaviest remote-sensing satellite - built to watch its own land from space.

At 1,360 kg, it was India's heaviest and most advanced remote-sensing satellite at the time, placed into a polar sun-synchronous orbit roughly 817 kilometres above Earth.

Its LISS-3, LISS-4 and AWiFS sensors extended and upgraded the data India's earlier IRS satellites had been providing - designed for a 5-year mission life, used for agriculture, water resources and land-use planning.

A satellite built to monitor India's crops, water and land use gave planners and farmers data that didn't depend on any other country's satellite program.
